title: Book notes
audience: For readers who want to remember more than the cover a year later.
description: Send highlights as you read. Your AI keeps the quotes, the big idea and what you'll do differently.
tagline: The big idea and the lines worth keeping.
note:
Book notes

What stuck from each book: the big idea, the lines worth keeping, and what you'll do differently. Newest book first.

## Books

prompt.default: Use my Pinto Notes note "Book notes". Read it with fetch before each change. When I start a book, add a heading for it at the start of "Books" with edit, like "### Title by Author". As I send you highlights and thoughts, add them under that book's heading with edit: quotes as > quotes with the page number, my own thoughts as bullets. Keep my words; don't polish them. When I say I've finished, add "**The big idea:**" in three sentences and two to four things I'll do differently as a checklist.

### Four Thousand Weeks by Oliver Burkeman
> "The day will never arrive when you finally have everything under control." (p. 31)

- The to-do list is infinite by design. Finishing it isn't the goal.
- Pick your three big projects; everything else waits.

**The big idea:** life is short and attention is finite. Trying to do everything guarantees the important things get squeezed. Choose what to neglect, on purpose.

- [ ] Keep a list of three active projects, no more
- [ ] Do the most important thing first, before email

## Books
### Four Thousand Weeks by Oliver Burkeman
> "The day will never arrive when you finally have everything under control." (p. 31)

- The to-do list is infinite by design. Finishing it isn't the goal.
- Pick your three big projects; everything else waits.
- Saying no to good things is the hard part.
- Rest isn't a reward for finishing: nothing is ever finished.

**The big idea:** life is short and attention is finite. Trying to do everything guarantees the important things get squeezed. Choose what to neglect, on purpose.

- [ ] Keep a list of three active projects, no more
- [ ] Do the most important thing first, before email
- [ ] Keep one evening a week with nothing planned

### Deep Work by Cal Newport
- Two focused hours beat a scattered day.
- Shallow work gets a slot of its own, so it can't leak into the rest.

**The big idea:** attention is the thing to protect. Decide when the deep work happens before the day decides for you.
